sources.entry: Farol - Terminal built on libghostty that shows which coding agent is working, waiting or done. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/snowztech/farol) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Farol is a macOS terminal app built on libghostty that runs several coding agents side by side and shows which are working, waiting or done.
summary.what_it_does: Farol is a terminal for macOS that hosts multiple coding-agent sessions in a sidebar, with a status dot per session showing working, waiting for you, done, or idle. It reads agent state from Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi through one-click connections, or from any agent that calls the farol status command. It can create tasks that start an agent in a new git worktree, and it offers worktree sessions, split panes, a file tree with editing, a diff review panel, a git graph, and merge-conflict resolution. It also includes a menu bar or screen-edge status indicator, and an iPhone companion (in beta) that lists sessions and handles approvals through an end-to-end encrypted relay. It uses Ghostty's rendering and reads the user's Ghostty config, and it ships its own themes plus support for Ghostty's themes.
use_cases: run several coding agents in parallel terminals
see which AI agent is waiting for approval
start an agent on a Jira or GitHub issue in its own git worktree
review and commit changes an agent made
resolve git merge conflicts in a terminal UI
monitor agents from the macOS menu bar or iPhone
how_to_run: Download Farol.dmg from the latest release and drag Farol to Applications
make install # builds Farol into /Applications (from source, needs macOS 14+ and Xcode 26)
make run # quick debug build from source
stack: Zig 0.16 (optional, for building libghostty from source)
notable: Status dots and notifications show whether each coding agent is working, waiting or done, with one-click hook setup for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi
Worktree sessions and tasks give each agent its own git worktree and branch
Built on libghostty, so it renders like Ghostty and loads your Ghostty config
Built-in git graph, diff review, commit/push, and three-way merge conflict resolver
Companion iPhone app (TestFlight beta) for replying to agents remotely over an end-to-end encrypted relay
caveats: Early software; the README warns to expect rough edges
Requires a Mac with Apple Silicon and macOS 14 or later
iPhone app is in beta on TestFlight; farol-host remote runner is experimental
Agents run on the Mac, so it must stay awake unless you use farol-host on a server
keywords: work on several branches at once
